title: Slight changes of conditions and slight crosses both increase vigour and fertility

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Slight changes of conditions and slight crosses both increase vigour and fertility

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Slight changes in conditions of life benefit organisms, and crosses between slightly different members of the same species give vigour and fertility to offspring, whereas greater changes and wider crosses tend to cause sterility.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Hence it seems that, on the one hand, slight changes in the conditions of life benefit all organic beings, and on the other hand, that slight crosses, that is crosses between the males and females of the same species which have varied and become slightly different, give vigour and fertility to the offspring.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Parallelism between the effects of changed conditions of life and crossing”. Scope: plants and animals generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predicted hump-shaped relationships are testable in many experiments. Existing data do not adequately cover Darwin's universal scope or jointly measure both parallels.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate nonlinear responses of fitness and fertility to environmental displacement and parental genetic distance. Peaks at modest environmental change and modest outcrossing, with declines at extremes, support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Environmental and genetic effects are usually studied separately.

Optimal change depends strongly on taxon and baseline environment.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Each half can be proxied, heterosis with pedigrees and beneficial acclimation with transplant experiments, but they are not one analysis and the environmental half is scattered. The joint hump-shaped claim is only partly operational until 'slight' is given a scale. Existing open fitness pedigrees cover animals far better than the full scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Plot fitness against environmental distance from the parental environment, and offspring fitness against parental genetic or phenotypic distance. A benefit at slight distances and sterility or reduced vigor at large distances would support both clauses; monotonic harm from any change, or no heterosis at slight genetic distance, would count against the corresponding clause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Environmental-distance experiments and crossing experiments are different datasets and are rarely paired.

'All organic beings' is far broader than any public reaction-norm table.

Slight versus great is an undefined cutoff.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.5
